bias_notes: Current enriched sample is complaint-heavy and dominated by Play Store reviews.
Discovery-specific themes should be interpreted alongside this source bias.

hypotheses.hypothesis: If Instamart uses surface guarantees and post-order reassurance in adjacent-category prompts for Family Household users during replenishment missions, then new-category add-to-order rate among eligible users should improve for grocery opportunities.
hypotheses.user_problem: Family Household users do not want to try more categories when core grocery or delivery experiences feel unreliable.
hypotheses.proposed_intervention: Surface freshness or replacement guarantees near adjacent-category modules.
hypotheses.expected_effect: Higher trust should reduce drop-off from expansion prompts and increase willingness to try adjacent categories.
hypotheses.primary_metric: new-category add-to-order rate among eligible users
assumptions: Reliability concerns are suppressing exploration, not just driving churn.
Trust cues placed near expansion surfaces will change willingness to browse or add items.
The current sample is still dominated by Play Store complaints and should be treated as directional.

hypotheses.hypothesis: If Instamart uses show low-risk entry offers or bundles for adjacent categories for Habitual Replenisher users during replenishment missions, then trial conversion for promoted adjacent-category items should improve for grocery opportunities.
hypotheses.user_problem: Habitual Replenisher users hesitate to add new-category items because total cost feels uncertain or not worth the risk.
hypotheses.proposed_intervention: Bundle adjacent-category trials with staple reorder journeys.
hypotheses.expected_effect: Lower perceived risk should improve trial conversion in categories users already consider but do not purchase.
hypotheses.primary_metric: trial conversion for promoted adjacent-category items
assumptions: Users already have some intent but stop because economics are unclear.
Targeted offers will drive exploration without fully training users to wait for discounts.
The current sample is still dominated by Play Store complaints and should be treated as directional.

hypotheses.hypothesis: If Instamart uses improve discovery prompts and category navigation in high-intent journeys for Family Household users during replenishment missions, then share of users who open or add from a new category should improve for grocery opportunities.
hypotheses.user_problem: Family Household users stay in narrow replenishment missions because the app does not make new categories easy to find.
hypotheses.proposed_intervention: Add adjacent-category prompts during reorder and search journeys.
hypotheses.expected_effect: Better discovery should increase browse depth and new-category consideration without needing deep discounts.
hypotheses.primary_metric: share of users who open or add from a new category
assumptions: Users are willing to explore if relevant options are made visible at the right moment.
Discovery friction is a bigger constraint than supply for these themes.
The current sample is still dominated by Play Store complaints and should be treated as directional.
